headline: AI-capex reality check: GOOGL -3.5%, TSLA -4% AH on capex hikes + margin compression. Oil +4.5% on Iran Hormuz mining claim + Trump infrastructure threat. Brent within $2 of $100. Asia chips surged (KOSPI +3.9%) on Alphabet Cloud read-through.
client_frame: The Big Tech earnings we teed up yesterday delivered a textbook AI-capex reality check. Alphabet posted a genuinely blockbuster quarter — revenue $119.8B (+24% YoY, its twelfth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth), Google Cloud +82% to $24.8B (accelerating from +63% Q1 and blowing away the +64% consensus), operating margin expanding to 34%. And the stock is down 3.5% after hours. Two reasons: capital expenditures were $44.9B in the quarter (double year-ago), management raised the FY26 capex guide by $15B to $195-205B, and consolidated free cash flow went negative for the first time in company history at -$5.9B. Cloud backlog also jumped $50B QoQ to $514B, so the demand is unambiguously real, but the market re-tasked itself with a harder question: at what point does 'AI investment' stop being reinvestment and start being permanent margin destruction. Tesla is the same story from a much weaker starting point — revenue beat handsomely at $28.24B (biggest since Q2 2023), but operating margin collapsed to 1.4% versus 4.9% consensus, adjusted EPS came in at $0.33 versus $0.51 expected, and the call pivoted openly to 'AI-powered cars and robots' as the growth story. Stock -4% after-hours. ServiceNow was the counterpoint — AI ACV crossed $1B, subscription revenue +24.5% constant currency, full-year guide raised, stock +4.5% AH — reminding everyone that AI monetization at the software layer is working even while the infrastructure layer is spending itself into free cash flow negativity. Overnight, geopolitics compounded. Iran explicitly warned shipping companies that the southern Strait of Hormuz route has been mined — first explicit mining claim of the conflict. Trump threatened to bomb Iranian civilian energy infrastructure. Result: Brent +4.5% to $98.32 (within $2 of $100 for the first time since March), WTI +4.4% to $90.62, Murban (light Gulf grade) up 19% above $106 on a separate Red Sea disruption. This is the fifth consecutive up day for oil. The 10Y closed 4.657% Wednesday (+2.9bp), the highest of the entire conflict period. Sep FOMC hike odds pushed further hawkish overnight — cumulative +25bp cumulative hike into September now 78.4% and single most likely +25bp. Client framing for Thursday: this is the definitive test of whether the AI-capex trade can survive its own arithmetic. Netflix reports pre-market results have already been digested; today's after-close is Intel — the AI referendum for legacy semis, plus American Airlines, Honeywell, and Union Pacific pre-market. Overlaid on a live oil shock into a rate market that is drifting hawkish into a Fed meeting six days away. Positioning: yesterday's advice holds and gets stronger — do not chase this dip and do not chase the Alphabet bounce narrative on operational excellence alone. The market is repricing the risk that AI capex is not a value-creation exercise but a margin-destruction exercise. That repricing will not resolve in a single session, and the setup — Iranian escalation + hawkish rates + hyperscaler capex fatigue — is a genuine three-legged risk stool. Hedges paid handsomely on the GOOGL/TSLA gap-down; keep them on. Watch Brent through $100 as the critical technical/psychological level; sustained close above changes the Fed's inflation asymmetry ahead of Wednesday's decision.
